name: Cawthorne
landmarks: Cannon Hall Country Park, Farm & Museum
blurb: Calm, one-to-one home dog grooming a short drive north of Cawthorne. We groom one dog at a time in Hall Green, near Newmillerdam, and pick up plenty of S75 dogs fresh off the Cannon Hall parkland.
metaDescription: Dog groomer near Cawthorne (S75)? Keith's K9 Care is a calm, one-dog-at-a-time home salon in Hall Green, Wakefield WF4 — about 15 minutes north. Book today.
lead: A fifteen-minute drive north of the Cannon Hall parkland, Keith's K9 Care is a calm, one-to-one home dog grooming salon in Hall Green — and we groom a good number of Cawthorne dogs who come back caked in country mud.
body: Cawthorne sits over the boundary in Barnsley (S75), out west towards the A635 and the edge of the M1, with Cannon Hall Country Park, Farm and the village museum on its doorstep. It's a quiet, well cared-for village, so the dogs here tend to walk a lot — and that shows in their coats. The run up to us in Hall Green takes about fifteen minutes and roughly five and a half miles, heading north towards Newmillerdam and the Wakefield boundary.

Those 70 acres of parkland at Cannon Hall are a gift and a problem in equal measure. The lakes, the walled garden, the long grass and the woods are made for a proper romp, but a wet spaniel or a doodle comes home with half of it stuck to the legs and belly. The same goes for the conifer tracks through Deffer Wood and the field paths over towards High Hoyland and Silkstone. That kind of mud works its way deep into a thick coat, and a quick bath at home rarely shifts it for long.

This is where a calm, unhurried groom earns its keep. I work on my own, one dog at a time, from a home salon at 4 Castle Meadows — no kennels, no row of cages, no other dogs barking through the wall. Your dog comes in, gets my full attention, and goes home. For a nervy rescue or a pup having a first groom, that quiet makes a real difference compared with a busy high-street place. I trained at Mrs B's Grooming Academy in Leeds and I'm IPET-qualified, so the handling is careful and the finish is honest.

Prices are on the website and there are no surprises at the door. A full groom runs from £40 for a small dog, £50 for a medium and £60 for a large breed or a doodle; a bath and tidy starts at £30, a puppy's first groom from £25, and de-matting or hand stripping from £50. Parking is straight outside on Castle Meadows, so there's no faff at the end of a country drive. To book, call or message Keith on 07926 471552 and we'll sort a time that works.

faqs.q: How far is the salon from Cawthorne?
faqs.a: About five and a half miles — roughly a fifteen-minute drive north up towards Hall Green in Wakefield (WF4). You head out of the village and up towards Newmillerdam, and we're on Castle Meadows with parking right outside.

faqs.q: My dog gets filthy at Cannon Hall — can you sort that out?
faqs.a: Yes, that's a lot of what I do. The parkland, lakes and woods leave coats matted with mud, and a bath and tidy or a full groom clears it down to the skin. If the coat has matted badly, de-matting starts at £50, and I'll always tell you honestly what the coat needs.

faqs.q: Do you cover Cawthorne and the rest of S75?
faqs.a: I do. Plenty of my dogs come from Cawthorne and the villages around it — Silkstone, High Hoyland, Barugh Green and Kexbrough. It's an easy run north, and the quiet, one-to-one groom is worth the short drive out of the village.

faqs.q: How do I book, and what are your hours?
faqs.a: Call or message Keith on 07926 471552 and we'll find a slot that suits you. Because it's one dog at a time, days fill up, so it's worth booking ahead — especially after a wet spell when half of Cawthorne needs a clean-up. I'll confirm the time and the price when you get in touch.

faqs.q: My dog is nervous or a rescue — will that be a problem?
faqs.a: Not at all, and the calm setup helps. There's only ever one dog in the salon, so there's no pack of other dogs, no noise and no rush. I take nervous and rescue dogs at their own pace, and for some that means we build it up over a couple of visits rather than forcing a full groom on day one.

faqs.q: Is it really calmer than a normal grooming salon?
faqs.a: Yes. Many high-street salons run several dogs through at once, with cages and constant barking. Here it's just me in a home salon, one dog at a time, no kennels. For a dog that finds the Cannon Hall crowds and a busy groomer too much, that quieter setting tends to make the whole thing easier.
